title: que eu fale
intro: The subjunctive (conjuntivo) is a set of verb forms used mostly after que, for wishes, doubts and feelings: *Quero que venhas* = I want you to come.
Good news: you already know these forms from commands. Take the *eu* form of the present, drop the -o and swap the vowel: *falo* → *fale*, *como* → *coma*, *faço* → *faça*, *venho* → *venha*.

tables.meaning: to eat (-ir verbs work the same: abra)
tables.caption: Present subjunctive of comer

examples.en: I want you to come.
I hope you're well.
Maybe it'll rain tomorrow.
You need to know this.

notes: *Espero que estejas bem* is a standard way to start a message to a friend.

drills.en: I want you to come.
I hope you're well.
Maybe it'll rain tomorrow.
You need to know this.
I don't think it's a good idea.
I hope you have a good weekend.

title: quero que, talvez, embora
summary: when to use the present subjunctive
intro: Use it after que when the first verb is about a wish or request (querer que, pedir que, preferir que, esperar que), doubt (duvidar que, *não acho* que) or need (*é preciso* que, *é importante* que).
Also after *talvez* (maybe) and some linking words: *para* que (so that), *embora* (although), *antes* que (before), *até* que (until), *caso* (in case).
Not after certainty: *Acho que ele vem* (I think he's coming) uses the normal present. *Não acho que ele venha* (I don't think he's coming) uses the subjunctive.

examples.en: I'm asking you to speak more slowly.
I doubt he knows.
Although I'm tired, I'm going out.

examples.pt: Leva o casaco, caso faça frio.
examples.en: Take your coat in case it's cold.

notes: Quick test: are you stating a fact (*acho* que, *sei* que, *é verdade* que)? Normal present. Is it wished, doubted, needed or uncertain? Subjunctive.
If it's the same person, use the infinitive instead: *Quero ir* (I want to go), but *Quero que vás* (I want you to go).

drills.en: I think he's coming.
drills.why: *Acho* que states what you believe: normal present.

drills.en: I don't think he's coming.
I want you to go with me.
drills.why: A wish about someone else: *quero* que + subjunctive.

drills.en: I know she's right.
drills.why: *Sei* que states a fact: normal present.

drills.en: I doubt she's right.
Although I'm tired, I'm going out.
Take your coat in case it's cold.
I want to go to the cinema.
drills.why: The same person wants and goes: just the infinitive.

drills.en: I'll explain again so that you understand.
It's true that they live in Lisbon.
drills.why: *É verdade* que states a fact: normal present.

drills.en: It's important that you arrive on time.
Maybe you're right.
drills.why: *Talvez* before the verb takes the subjunctive.

title: se eu fosse
summary: the imperfect subjunctive: if I were, if I had
intro: Take the *eles* form of the simple past, drop -ram and add -sse: *falaram* → *falasse*, *fizeram* → *fizesse*, *foram* → *fosse*. Endings: -sse, -sses, -sse, -ssemos, -ssem (*nós* has an accent: *falássemos*).
Use it for imaginary or unlikely conditions with se: *Se eu tivesse tempo*, *ia contigo* = If I had time, I'd go with you.
And where the present subjunctive would go, when the sentence is in the past: *Quero que venhas* → *Queria que viesses* (I wanted you to come). *Como* se (as if) always takes it.

examples.pt: Se eu fosse rico, viajava pelo mundo.
examples.en: If I were rich, I'd travel the world.
If I had time, I'd go with you.
I wanted you to come to the party.
He talks as if he knew everything.

notes: For the "would" part, Portugal usually uses the imperfeito (*ia*, *viajava*). The conditional (iria, viajaria) sounds more formal.
*Quem me dera* que…! = If only…! *Quem me dera que fosse sexta-feira*!

drills.en: If I were rich, I'd travel the world.
If I had time, I'd go with you.
I wanted you to come to the party.
He talks as if he knew everything.
If I could, I'd help you.
If only it were Friday!

title: quando fores
summary: the future subjunctive: when you go, if you can
intro: Portuguese has a future subjunctive, and Portugal uses it all the time. It's for something that may happen later, after *quando* (when), se (if), *assim* que (as soon as), *enquanto* (while, as long as), *sempre* que (whenever), and o que / *quem* / *como* (whatever, whoever, however).
Take the *eles* form of the simple past and drop -am: *falaram* → *falar*, *fizeram* → *fizer*, *foram* → for. Endings: -, -es, -, -mos, -em.
For regular verbs it looks like the infinitive: *quando chegares*, *se falarmos*.

tables.caption: Future subjunctive of ser and ir

examples.en: When you go to Lisbon, call me.
If you can, come to dinner.
As soon as I arrive, I'll let you know.
Do as you like.

notes: Compare: *Se tens tempo* (if you have time, right now) and Se tiveres *tempo* (if you have time, later on). For plans, Portugal very often uses the second.
Careful: *vir* (to come) → *vier*, and *ver* (to see) → *vir*. *Quando vires a Ana* = When you see Ana.
*Como queiras* (as you like) is also very common.

drills.en: When you go to Lisbon, call me.
If you can, come to dinner.
As soon as I arrive, I'll let you know.
Do as you like.
When you see Ana, say hello to her.
If the weather's good, we'll go to the beach.

title: venha, viesse or vier?
intro: Present subjunctive (*venha*): wishes, doubts and needs about now or the future, after *quero* que, *espero* que, *talvez*, *embora*…
Imperfect subjunctive (*viesse*): imaginary conditions (*se eu fosse*…), *como* se, and when the first verb is in the past (*queria* que…).
Future subjunctive (*vier*): something that may happen later, after *quando*, se, *assim* que, *enquanto*…

examples.en: I want you to come tomorrow.
I wanted you to come yesterday.

examples.pt: Se tiver dinheiro, compro uma casa.
examples.en: If I have money, I'll buy a house.

examples.pt: Se tivesse dinheiro, comprava uma casa.
examples.en: If I had money, I'd buy a house.

notes: Se + future subjunctive is a real possibility (it may happen). Se + imperfect subjunctive is imaginary or unlikely.

drills.en: I hope you're well.
If I had money, I'd buy a house.
drills.why: Imaginary (I don't have it): imperfect subjunctive.

drills.en: If I have money, I'll buy a house.
drills.why: A real possibility later on: future subjunctive.

drills.en: When you go to Lisbon, call me.
I want you to come tomorrow.
I wanted you to come yesterday.
Maybe I'll arrive late.
As soon as I have news, I'll tell you.
He talks as if he were the boss.
drills.why: *Como* se (as if) always takes the imperfect subjunctive.

drills.en: Although it's cold, I'm going to the beach.
If only it were summer!
drills.why: *Quem me dera* que takes the imperfect subjunctive.

drills.en: Call me when you're home.
